title: Art Therapists
description: Plan or conduct art therapy sessions or programs to improve clients' physical, cognitive, or emotional well-being.

tasks.text: Design art therapy sessions or programs to meet client's goals or objectives.
Develop individualized treatment plans that incorporate studio art therapy, counseling, or psychotherapy techniques.
Write treatment plans, case summaries, or progress or other reports related to individual clients or client groups.
Customize art therapy programs for specific client populations, such as those in schools, nursing homes, wellness centers, prisons, shelters, or hospitals.
Establish goals or objectives for art therapy sessions in consultation with clients or site administrators.
Coordinate art showcases to display artwork produced by clients.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with other professionals on client's treatment team to develop, coordinate, or integrate treatment plans.
Communicate client assessment findings and recommendations in oral, written, audio, video, or other forms.
Coordinate field trips for client groups to museums or other public displays of art.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Assess client needs or disorders, using drawing, painting, sculpting, or other artistic processes.
Interpret the artistic creations of clients to assess their functioning, needs, or progress.
Analyze or synthesize client data to draw conclusions or make recommendations for art therapy.
Analyze data to determine the effectiveness of treatments or therapy approaches.
Instruct individuals or groups in the use of art media, such as paint, clay, or yarn.
Teach art therapy techniques or processes to artists, interns, volunteers, or others.
Observe and document client reactions, progress, or other outcomes related to art therapy.
Conduct art therapy sessions, providing guided self-expression experiences to help clients recover from, or cope with, cognitive, emotional, or physical impairments.
Talk with clients during art or other therapy sessions to build rapport, acknowledge their progress, or reflect upon their reactions to the artistic process.
Select or prepare artistic media or related equipment or devices to accomplish therapy session objectives.
Recommend or purchase needed art supplies or equipment.
Supervise staff, volunteers, practicum students, or interns.
Gather client information from sources such as case documentation, client observation, or interviews of client or family members.
Review research or literature in art therapy, psychology, or related disciplines.
Conduct information sharing sessions, such as in-service workshops for other professionals, potential client groups, or the general community.
Photograph or videotape client artwork for inclusion in client records or for promotional purposes.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Autodesk Maya.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat.

skills.name: Video creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to enable production of video content. Examples: Adobe After Effects.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
